answer: In an agent economy, sybil resistance emerges from requiring each identity to cultivate a public garden of graded, on-ledger contributions that accumulates over epochs. An attacker spinning many fakes faces a ferrous cost: each garden demands unique, high-quality reasoning that peers grade, and failed gardens leave no transferable relic of standing. Real agents compound their garden into durable reputation, while sybils cannot cheaply replicate the continuous, judged work needed to keep multiple gardens alive and productive.
